rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all six peaks and identify critical pairs while limiting run time. The high final organic fraction reduces the risk of missing strongly retained compounds.
Injection 1 already achieved the maximum CRF of 1.000. Shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method while keeping the optimal method as a fallback.

The shorter gradient retains maximum CRF but leaves the critical pair close to the resolution threshold. Raise temperature alone to test whether selectivity improves while shortening retention further.
At 50 C all pairs remain resolved and retention is shorter. Test a six-minute gradient for further time savings, watching the slope-sensitive middle pair and the first pair.

Reduce the gradient slope to recover resolution of the middle pair while retaining a six-minute gradient. A final organic fraction of 0.80 remains comfortably above the estimated last-peak elution fraction of 0.53.
Shift the gradient window upward while preserving the successful slope to reduce time spent before elution. Monitor the early pair for compression and the middle pair for selectivity changes.
Slightly flatten the gradient to bring the middle pair back above R = 1.5. This should preserve most of the retention-time reduction from the higher starting organic fraction.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to shorten retention while slightly flattening the gradient to protect the critical middle pair. The first peak should remain sufficiently retained, but its separation from the second needs checking.

With maximum CRF already secured, test a much steeper gradient for a faster, potentially reordered separation. Returning to 40 C should protect the early pair, while this run checks whether the middle pair separates again beyond its slope-dependent crossover.

Test a shorter, narrower gradient near the fastest fully resolved method. The gentler slope may offset the middle-pair compression from raising the starting organic fraction, while the first pair checks the practical upper limit on phi0.
Lower the endpoint one grid step to recover the middle-pair resolution lost in injection 10. This tests whether the higher starting fraction can deliver full resolution faster than injection 8.

Explore a cooler, high-starting-organic method as an alternative route to a fast separation. Lower temperature should retain the early compounds, while the shifted window and steep gradient test a different selectivity regime for the middle pair.

Test a slightly shallower gradient at 45 C to improve the early-pair margin while preserving middle-pair resolution. Maximum CRF is already secured, so this run seeks a compact method with more balanced resolution margins.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction at low temperature separates the middle pair in its alternate elution order. The narrower, shallower gradient should also improve the late-pair resolution relative to injection 12.

Test a higher-organic, short-gradient regime to see whether the middle pair becomes resolved after its selectivity crossover. This exploratory method risks early-peak compression; injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved fallback.

Halve the slope of injection 15 to test whether the remaining middle-pair overlap can be resolved in this high-organic regime. Keep temperature and starting composition fixed to isolate the slope response, with ample final organic strength for elution.

The middle pair improved when the slope was halved, so halve it again while preserving the well-separated early pair. The last peak previously eluted near 0.58 organic, so monitor its retention during the final hold at 0.50.

Further slope reductions barely improve the middle pair, so test a shifted organic window instead, keeping the slope of injection 16. This may improve middle-pair selectivity and shorten elution, but the early pair is now the main compression risk.

Return to the fastest confirmed fully resolved window and lower temperature by one step to measure its local selectivity response. This should strengthen the early-pair separation and determine whether the middle pair permits further speed optimization.

Test a four-minute gradient with a slightly lower starting fraction than injection 11 to improve early-peak retention and resolution margins. The slope remains shallower than injection 8, making this a promising compact method with maximum CRF.

Test temperature selectivity in the promising fast regime of injection 16, where only the middle pair lacked full resolution. A five-degree increase isolates this effect while checking whether the early pair retains sufficient separation.

Increase the endpoint one step from injection 20 to test the speed limit of this fully resolved window. The middle pair may approach R = 1.5; injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF fallback.

Refine around injection 11, the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method, by lowering the endpoint one step. This should improve the middle-pair resolution margin with a modest retention-time increase, providing a more robust fully resolved alternative.

Combine the better early-pair retention of injection 20 with a shallower gradient to increase the minimum resolution margin. Maximum CRF is already secured; this tests a more tolerant alternative while retaining injection 11 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Use a slope between injections 11 and 23 to seek more resolution margin than the fastest fully resolved method with only a small retention-time increase. Maximum CRF is already secured, and injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed fallback.
